Why Choi Yu Ree turns to nature in “Forest”

Choi explains how natural imagery lets her approach painful relationships indirectly, giving feelings of inadequacy the shape of a smaller tree.

BY indiek / 2026-11-15

The release note for Choi Yu Ree’s “Forest” begins with a difference in height: a small tree stands among people imagined as taller trees, their lives seemingly going well. That comparison gives feeling inadequate a visible shape. [Release notes on Genie](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=82923028). [2]

In Sa Ji-won’s September 2024 interview for Dong-A Ilbo, Choi connected the song to feelings of inadequacy around others during university. Asked about writing “Forest”, she explained that she borrows from nature to address things beyond her control, including human relationships. Speaking directly about relationships hurts, she said, so she approaches them indirectly. Her explanation gives a specific purpose to the trees: they let her speak about a difficult experience through an image. [Sa Ji-won’s interview, syndicated on Daum](https://v.daum.net/v/20240920030416504?s=print_news). [1]

“Forest” (숲) appeared on 유영, released on August 24, 2022. Choi wrote the lyrics and composed the song, sharing the arrangement credit with Moon Ji-hyuk (문지혁). [Release record and credits](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=82923028). [2]

The release note also expresses a wish to grow and live among the other trees. The people who make the small tree feel inadequate are the very people it wants to join. Belonging remains a desire here: the image holds both the painful comparison and the wish for company. [Release notes on Genie](https://www.genie.co.kr/detail/albumInfo?axnm=82923028). [2]
